To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) PB stimulates liver growth by induction of hypertrophy and inhibition apoptosis in c-myc transgenic mice; (2) the inhibition of apoptosis is brought about by a reduction of TGF-beta signaling and increase in Bcl-xL expression; (3) the induction of hypertrophy is associated with an increase in BCL-2 expression; and (4) the induction of BCL-2 and BCL-xL is independent of TGF-alpha overexpression
the liver growth response to the non-genotoxic liver carcinogen phenobarbital in c-myc/ TGF-alpha transgenic mouse is due to inhibition of apoptosis and induction of liver hypertrophic growth.

phenobarbital (a widely used liver tumor promoter) promotes liver growth in transgenic mice over expressing both the c-mic and TGF-alpha genes by inducing hypertrophy, inhibiting apoptosis and decreasing the expression of TGF-beta ligand.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of action of phenobarbital in the liver, with the aim of understanding its role in the development of liver cancer.
the study of the mechanism of liver tumor promotion.
elucidation of the molecular mechanism by which PB promotes liver tumor formation in mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the PB-induced liver enlargement was due to an increased rate of hepatocyte growth in the early phase of treatment and to hypertrophy of the hepatocytes in the later phase of treatment, with a reduction in apoptosis throughout the period of PB treatment.
PB promotes neoplasm by inducing hypertrophy of hepatocytes and by inhibiting apoptosis.
phenobarbital is a non-genotoxically acting tumor promoter, that acts by inhibiting apoptosis and promoting hypertrophy of the hepatocyte.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

PB is an effective liver promoter, and the mechanism of action is to induce hypertrophy and to inhibit apoptosis, and that this is achieved by decreasing the level of TGF-beta and increasing the level of Bcl-2.

the c-myc/TG-alpha transgene is not sufficient to promote hepatocarcinogenesis and the PB is required for this to occur, but that it does so by promoting liver growth by a combination of mechanisms, including induction of hypertrophy and inhibition apoptosis.
PB induces liver hypertrophy and inhibits apoptosis, both of which contribute to the promotion of liver tumors in c-myc/ TGF-alpha transgenic mouse model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of transgenic mice to investigate the mechanisms of action of carcinogens is a powerful approach.
the liver growth induced by phenobarbital is a result of both an induction of cell proliferation and an inhibition of cell death.
the promotion of hepatocarcinogenesis by PB is associated with the inhibition of apoptosis, which in turn is associated with an increase in BCL2 expression and a reduction in TGF-beta signaling.
